basis: Inherited mitochondrial myopathy; CNS dysfunction is common (developmental delay 1/1, basal ganglia lesions 1/2); hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 1/2. Apnea does not establish intrinsic lung damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay 1/1 and basal ganglia lesions 1/2 support common CNS injury; supplied ancestry defines metabolic disease and myopathy.

basis: Historical hepatic glycogen storage I subtype with impaired glucose homeostasis; renal functional damage affecting >=30% is not established for this subtype.

decisions.renal: none: no subtype-specific evidence establishes renal functional damage in >=30%; renal deposition alone is insufficient.

basis: Intellectual disability and progressive skeletal abnormalities define disease; hypodontia/dental defects occur in 80-99%; hearing impairment is annotated in 1/1, with substantial sampling uncertainty.

decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment is documented in 1/1 assessed; supplied HPO frequency supports inclusion, although the small denominator limits confidence.

basis: Inherited defects of hepatic bilirubin conjugation or excretion establish metabolic and hepatic localization; neurologic injury and renal disease are subtype-specific.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic bilirubin processing or excretion is the affected organ function across the usual subtypes; primary localization does not require hepatocyte destruction.

basis: OXPHOS disorder with Leigh encephalopathy and cardiomyopathy; skeletal myopathy is explicitly defining in supplied synonyms, qualifying without a numerical frequency; primary slots are full.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal myopathy is explicit in equivalent disease names, satisfying the defining-feature exception; three primary slots are already occupied.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; hypoplastic nails and sparse postpubertal hair are described as typical, supporting >=30% dermatologic involvement, although numerical frequencies are unavailable.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: nail hypoplasia and sparse hair are typical associated abnormalities, supporting >=30%; they are ancillary to the defining skeletal dysplasia.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disease; strabismus occurs in 3/7 (~43%). Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; osteopenia 3/7 lacks evidence of intrinsic bone disease independent of immobility or treatment.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: osteopenia in 3/7 meets the numerical threshold, but direct skeletal involvement is unproven; immobility and antiseizure treatment are plausible secondary causes.

basis: Sepsis directly causes acute renal dysfunction in roughly 35-50%, as part of its organ-failure syndrome. Transient hypotension does not establish cardiac damage; intrinsic myocardial injury varies.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypotension alone does not establish organ damage; intrinsic myocardial dysfunction is not securely >=30% across the full sepsis population.
decisions.renal: involved: direct sepsis-associated acute renal dysfunction affects roughly 35-50% and constitutes the disease's acute organ-failure syndrome.

basis: OXPHOS disorder with defining hepatic insufficiency and encephalopathy (1/2); hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 1/2. Muscle injury/rhabdomyolysis 1/2 also qualifies but is omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic insufficiency is explicitly part of the defining clinical description, establishing functional liver disease.
decisions.cardiovascular: involved: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy occurs in 1/2; primary slots prioritize metabolic disease, defining hepatic insufficiency and encephalopathy.

basis: The defining triad comprises hearing loss (6/7), congenital cardiovascular defects including pulmonary artery stenosis (5/7), and posterior embryotoxon (7/7).

decisions.ocular: primary: posterior embryotoxon is an explicit defining component of the named syndrome (7/7); primary diagnostic localization does not require visual impairment.
